english.title: Stalking involving serious alarm / distress
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) your course of conduct amounted to stalking and caused **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) serious alarm or distress, which had an adverse effect on

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

usual day-to-day activities when you knew or ought to have known that your course of conduct would cause alarm or distress to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) on each occasion in that **(..SPECIFY THE DATES, PLACES AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4A(1)(a)(b)(ii) and (5) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The maximum penalty on indictment was increased from five to ten years from 3rd April 2017, see H18818/PH97011 for offences committed on or after that date. That offence also applies where the conduct occurred over two or more days before and after that date, see section 175 of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.
(ii) Section 4A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 was inserted by section 111 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 with effect from 25/11/2012.
(iii) See section 4A(7) for an alternative verdict.
(iv) Incidents in cases of harassment must be so connected in type and in context as to justify the conclusion that they amounted to a course of conduct. See R v Patel [2004] EWCA Crim 3284
(v) Section 4A(2) and (3) regarding knowledge that a person's course of conduct will cause fear/alarm/distress.(vi) Section 4A(4) provides a defence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 12 months should be read as a reference to 6 months

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneOn the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
